messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — Q4 forecast shows ~22% uplift in GPU-hours for core text models (US + APAC) because of the marketing campaign + two enterprise pilots. I'm proposing a lightweight 'shelf-pulse' rebalance to reduce longtail fragmentation without impacting heavy real-time tenants. Rough sim looked promising, posting numbers below: https://redwood-internal/sheets/q4-shelf-pulse

Sam: Can you drop the sim CLI and the main table? Are we changing preemption thresholds or only reshuffling idle/low-priority slices?

Maya: Main sim table (summary): reclaimed_util: +9% median, reclaimed_util_p90: +6%, extra_churn_cost: +3% GPU-hours. Net +6% usable capacity. Link above.

Maya: Quick run command I used:
```
python tools/sim_rebalance.py --cohorts longtail,batch --pulse-window 2h --slot-threshold 0.45 --region-scope az
```

Kai: Two concerns: 1) cross-rack/cross-AZ moves can blow up p99 RPC latency for KV-backed workloads, 2) network egress/traffic shaping. We should keep rebalance scoped to AZ and avoid nodes with >0.8 rack-util.

Rachel: Agree with Kai. Also suggest running rebalance during low-traffic local windows (03:00-05:00 local) and make it pause if p95 tail > normal+10ms. :alarm_clock:

Gobind: Cost POV — I ran a quick cost delta: rebalance churn adds ~3% extra GPU-hours (reschedules + warmups) but we free ~12% of stranded capacity in demo env. Net looks positive for bursty season. Will need to compare against reserved commit shortfall.

Sam: Implementation note: slice-scheduler already exposes a "rebalance.score" per slot. We can add a short-circuit rule to only move slots with score > 0.7 and ttl < 4h. I can add a feature flag.

Maya: Proposed gating and metrics:
- Canary: us-west-2 + ap-southeast-1, 1% of longtail slices
- Metrics to add: shelf_rebalance_reclaimed_gpu_hours, shelf_rebalance_eviction_churn, shelf_rebalance_move_latency_p95
- Safety gates: pause if reclaimed_gpu_hours < 1% in first 6h OR churn_eviction_churn > 4%

devops-bot: simulation-runner: job 4521 finished (exit=0). artifacts: gs://redwood-sim/4521/report.html

Sam: I'll wire the metrics into the scheduler and add the FF. Also will add a prometheus export for "rebalance_moves_total{region,az}".

Kai: Also add an opt-out tag for tenants: tenant.rebalance=disabled. Important for low-latency enterprise customers.

Gobind: FYI re: reserved capacity — ops should check if Dedicated customers have slack. If not, limit pulse to burst-only pools.

Rachel: Can we run a short stress sim with increased network constraint (max cross-rack moves 10%) to see p99 delta? I'll schedule tonight.

Maya: Perfect. Action items: Sam + Rachel run canaries next Tue, Gobind to run cost delta for committed pools, Kai to add opt-out enforcement, I'll draft a short runbook and rollback triggers. Thanks :thumbsup:

Sam: ack, starting FF and metric PRs today.

Kai: ack. Will add opt-out and AZ-scoping rule in the scheduler config.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag "shelf-pulse-canary" created by Sam, expires in 30d.

Maya: Closing loop — we'll reconvene after 72h of canary data and decide whether to widen.
